title: Plato's Republic
examples: What does Plato mean when he talks about the three parts of the soul?
How is the rule of philosopher kings different from modern democracy?
Can a society truly be just if some people have all the power?

explain.say: Plato's Republic explores what a just society should look like. He suggests that justice is about balance within the city.
Plato divides the city into three parts, just like the human soul. These parts are the rulers, the guardians, and the workers.
The rulers, or philosopher kings, must rule because they alone understand the true Forms. They seek knowledge, not just power.
The ideal city requires that each class performs its proper job. This specialization creates true justice for everyone.

draw.text: Justice: Each part does its job

explain.say: In everyday life, a just community needs people who are good at different things. A doctor needs to heal, and a farmer needs to grow food.

draw.text: Real Life: Specialization makes life work

explain.say: A common mistake is thinking everyone should rule equally. Plato argues that skill and knowledge determine who should lead.

items: Correct: Rule must match deep knowledge.

faq.q: Why does Plato think only philosophers should rule?
faq.a: Plato believed that only those who truly understand what is good and just can govern well. He felt that rulers needed deep knowledge, not just popular support.
asks: Who has the right to rule according to Plato?
Why must the wisest people be in charge?

faq.q: What is the difference between justice in the city and justice in a person?
faq.a: In the city, justice is when each class does its specific job. In a person, it is when the reason controls the spirit and appetites.
asks: How does the soul relate to the city?
Is personal justice the same as civic justice?

faq.q: Does Plato suggest that people should have private property?
faq.a: No, for the ruling classes, Plato suggests they should have no private property or families. This prevents them from becoming corrupt or attached to wealth.
asks: What happens to the rulers' possessions?

faq.q: What does 'The Forms' mean in this context?
faq.a: The Forms are the perfect, unchanging blueprints of things, like the perfect idea of Justice itself. The philosopher's job is to grasp these perfect ideas.
asks: What are the perfect ideas Plato talks about?
What is the concept of 'The Forms'?

faq.q: Is the ideal city something that can actually exist?
faq.a: This is a philosophical idea, so it is more of a model for thinking. It shows what a perfectly balanced society might look like in theory.
asks: Can we build this city today?

facts: Plato argued that the ideal state must mirror the structure of the just soul.
The philosopher kings are those who grasp the Form of the Good.
In Plato's view, the ruling class should own no private property.
Justice is achieved when each part performs its natural function.

quiz.say: According to Plato, who should hold the primary power in the ideal city?
quiz.why: They are the only ones who understand the true knowledge of the Good.

wrong.0: Strength alone does not equal wisdom or understanding.
wrong.1: The public often makes decisions based on emotion, not truth.
wrong.3: They are tempted by money, which can cloud true judgment.

quiz.say: If the city is like a person, what part represents the appetites or desires?
quiz.why: The workers represent the appetitive part that needs sustenance and physical goods.

wrong.0: The center is the whole, not one specific part.
wrong.2: The rulers represent the highest, most rational part of the soul.
wrong.3: The guardians represent the spirited, protective part of the soul.

quiz.say: What is the main source of 'justice' in Plato's Republic?

options.show: Each class fulfilling its natural role
options.say: Each class fulfilling its natural role

options.show: The king having all the power
options.say: The king having all the power

quiz.why: Justice is the harmony created when every part does what it is best suited for.

wrong.0: Excessive wealth can corrupt the necessary balance.
wrong.2: Military strength is only one part of a just society.
wrong.3: Plato argues that power must be balanced by wisdom.
